text: I always find it very uncomfortable and I always find it very pitiful to see very strong Singaporeans queuing up at the F&B outlets to collect the food for delivery.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I always wonder: such a strong, able-bodied Singaporean, why is he not doing other work?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: How many Singaporeans have actually come back as a general construction worker?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Of course, I would expect Singaporeans to be able to be trained for doing work like bricklaying and all that —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, could you just ask the clarifications, please?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The third question is, if the answers to both the first and the two questions are along the line that is positive, then I would agree that I will support of the Bill and the Government can act according to its discretion to bring in the foreign workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development and Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Is the hon Member saying that all our Singaporean delivery persons should become construction workers?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development and Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I was just trying to understand; is that what the Member is saying?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think some Singaporeans – because there are like about 100,000 gig workers in Singapore – and then, there are also Singaporeans who are unemployed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Given this COVID-19 environment now, if you raise the wages high enough, there is a threshold that I think Singaporeans will come in, even as a general construction worker.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And he is focusing principally on those who are doing food delivery.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach is in recognition that the processes need to be significantly re-orientated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The processes need to be changed and enhanced in order to create a good job for Singaporeans – a job which commands the level of productivity and skills that warrant the kinds of pay that I think the Member is talking about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: He does not have a figure but he is talking about increasing the pay until a threshold where Singaporeans come in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Whereas for him, he thinks if you increase the pay, Singaporeans, including delivery drivers and riders, will do the jobs that current workers from India, Bangladesh and other source countries are doing, as they are.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But what we are saying is that, yes, we need to pay the Singaporean more, but the job has to be different and it is not just as the Member suggests – architects, engineers or consultants but even builders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I visited once an Integrated Construction and Prefabrication Hub (ICPH), which is a precast hub yard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are actually building rooms, building panels for construction and Singaporeans are doing those jobs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But it is very different from the kind of job that the Member envisions Singaporeans will be doing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I seek the Members' support for this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I had erroneously stated that the Member Gerald Giam had indicated earlier that he had suggested permitting worker transfers from the 56th day onwards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Gerald had shared with me that he plans to advance this proposal but has not, in fact, done so in this House.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, I wish to clarify this for the record.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In terms of a quick clarification question for the Minister, I thank him for his clear articulation of efforts via the ITM to transform the sector by allowing costs to rise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: As he rightly pointed out, I am fully in support of this general principle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I should also note that we spent many hours earlier debating over what seems to anyone not in the industry to be a severe reluctance to even entertain a small escalation in the transportation cost of construction workers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, my question then is whether the Minister believes that the construction ITM has truly made headway in changing mindsets and behaviours and, if not, what is the timeline for which we can expect an actual change such that we will see increases in wages?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And there are opportunities then for Singaporeans to come into the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And not just raise the wages of the foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are studying how to make those moves to push the sector to be more lean.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are pushing on multiple fronts, not just on worker numbers and quotas; not just in making it expensive to construct.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But it has to be more productive and command better salaries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member spoke earlier about a proposal that his colleague Mr Gerald Giam did not yet make to this House.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a proposal, I presume, we will be expecting shortly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And I presume MOM will be looking forward to that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I remember the Member saying in his speech that it is important to retain the existing foreign workers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Given the worker shortage, I think both Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and we in the Government feel that it is important for employers to work with their existing foreign workers, look at their remuneration, look at their work conditions and, of course, find ways to encourage them to continue to stay in the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member talked about, well, SCMX is one, which is actually SCAL's effort to help to provide a marketplace for workers within Singapore so that they move employers, rather than be sent back.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But his proposal – or what he says is Mr Gerald Giam's upcoming proposal – is to, in effect, make it easier for workers to move from one employer to another.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You have a worker working with you, suddenly he is gone and it is because of moves and flexibilities which now the Member would like to enhance that will probably exacerbate this worker poaching.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MOM and SCAL's approach is different, recognising that the rule that the Member talks about was for a different time and a different era.
